CISA Issues Urgent Warning for Critical "Java4Shell" RCE Flaw

CRITICAL

CISA Urges Patching for Critical Java4Shell RCE Vulnerability

A critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed "Java4Shell," has been discovered in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder, affecting versions 17.0.6+ on specific x86-64 CPUs. The flaw, rated 9.2 CVSS, allows for unauthenticated RCE and impacts major enterprise applications like Jira, Confluence, and Jenkins. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued an urgent advisory for organizations to apply patches immediately.

Pentagon Mandates AI Training for All Cybersecurity Personnel

INFORMATIONAL

Pentagon Requires AI Training for Cyber Workforce

The U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) has announced that artificial intelligence training will become a mandatory requirement for its entire cybersecurity workforce. This move aims to equip defense personnel with the skills needed to counter increasingly sophisticated AI-driven threats from adversaries. The new policy is part of a broader shift towards skills-based hiring to address a significant shortage of 24,000 cyber professionals.

Russian APT Star Blizzard Uses Stolen Data for New Attack

The Russian FSB-linked APT group Star Blizzard (also known as Cold River and UNC4057) is weaponizing data stolen from a previous victim to launch new attacks. The initial compromise was achieved using MFA fatigue attacks.

CRITICAL

Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Flaw Under Active Attack

A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2026-115731, in Perforce Puppet's infrastructure management platform is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw, rated 9.4 CVSS, is an untrusted data deserialization issue that allows a client with any CA-signed certificate to execute code on the Puppet server, potentially leading to a full infrastructure compromise.

Microsoft's Record Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws, Including Outlook Zero-Day

CRITICAL

Microsoft Patches Exploited Outlook Zero-Day CVE-2026-124194

Microsoft has released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday update, addressing a record-breaking 1,235 vulnerabilities across its products. The most critical fix is for CVE-2026-124194, an actively exploited zero-day spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook. The flaw allows attackers to steal NTLM authentication hashes with a single click from a victim, bypassing security warnings. CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating a patch for federal agencies by November 24.

Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack Injects Malicious Code into 178 Major Websites

HIGH

Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack Compromises BBC, CNN, Zoom

A large-scale supply-chain attack compromised 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, and Zoom, by injecting malicious JavaScript via the Optimizely web experimentation platform. The malware, served from Optimizely's own CDN, was designed to skim payment card details, steal cryptocurrency, and deliver exploits to iPhones. The incident highlights the significant risks posed by third-party service compromises, allowing attackers to target visitors of trusted, high-traffic websites.

FBI Warns of ARTEX, an AI-Powered Tool for Autonomous Cyberattacks

HIGH

FBI Issues Alert on ARTEX AI-Powered Hacking Framework

The FBI has issued a FLASH advisory about ARTEX, an open-source, AI-driven penetration testing framework being weaponized by threat actors. The tool automates complex cyberattacks by translating natural language goals into machine-executable actions. It has been used in attacks against finance, government, and healthcare sectors globally, with some intrusions achieving privileged access in under three hours. The advisory signals a new era of autonomous, machine-speed attacks, lowering the barrier for less-skilled actors and accelerating campaigns.

Critical Apache Axis RCE Flaw Actively Exploited in N-able, Atlassian

CRITICAL

Critical Apache Axis RCE Flaw (CVE-2026-90436) Exploited

A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2026-90436, in the end-of-life Apache Axis library is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw, rated CVSS 9.8, affects enterprise products that use the library, including Atlassian Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central. Security firm Rapid7 has confirmed exploitation, and with a proof-of-concept available, organizations are urged to apply vendor patches on an emergency basis to mitigate the immediate threat of system compromise.

Microsoft Warns of Phishing Campaign Impersonating M365 Notifications

MEDIUM

Microsoft 365 Phishing Campaign Uses Outage Lures

Microsoft Threat Intelligence is tracking a high-volume credential phishing campaign that impersonates legitimate Microsoft 365 service health notifications. Detected on November 13, 2026, the emails use social engineering, creating a false sense of urgency by claiming a service outage has occurred and that messages will be deleted unless the user clicks a link to "restore" them. The campaign's primary goal is to steal user credentials for subsequent attacks.
